# Hand-authored chart fixtures

These synthetic, redistributable test inputs were authored for Wormedit and contain no copied commercial chart data or audio. Filenames such as `fixture.ogg`, `bgm-a.wav`, and `background.jpg` in chart text are intentional resource references; those specific resources are not bundled. A separate set of generated audio-only assets is documented in [`audio/README.md`](audio/README.md). The fixture corpus records input semantics and capability expectations, not a claim that a reader or writer is already implemented.

## Expected semantics and capability inventory

| Fixture | Expected semantic result / purpose | Current implementation/reference note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bms/repeated-bgm-ratio-stop-collision.bms` | Keep the two `#00001` statements as ordered, distinct BGM lanes, each with five structural slots. Their non-empty objects are at slots 0 and 3/5 in lane 1, and slot 2/5 in lane 2. Keep the playable object at slot 4/5. Measure 000 has exact length `3/4`; measure 001 has exact length `5/4`. At measure 000 row 0 retain the direct BPM 120, extended BPM 180, and STOP01 value 48 as three co-located source-ordered timing commands; STOP unit is the BMS 1/192-whole-note unit and is independent of the measure ratio. Defer effective collision precedence to the selected compatibility profile. | Loader evaluation currently converts to transient chart timing; the source command sequence, repeated BGM slot arrays, exact measure spelling, and BMS STOP definition provenance are not the editor contract and must be retained by Wormedit. See [`bms-command-memo.md`](../../docs/references/bms-command-memo.md). |
| `bms/control-flow-mixed.bms` | Preserve root/common content, RANDOM branches, IF/ELSEIF/ELSE, and SWITCH cases as an ordered tree. A selected RANDOM value of 1/2 selects its matching IF leaf; value 2 selects the ELSEIF leaf. For SWITCH value 1, execute CASE 1 and fall through CASE 2 until `#SKIP`; value 2 starts at CASE 2. Keep the nested RANDOM/IF inside CASE 1. | The byte parser retains every alternative and projects channel payloads when a caller supplies choices. Choice identity uses the physical opening-line order; nested channel payloads in unselected branches stay raw. See [`bms-control-flow.md`](../../docs/references/bms-control-flow.md). |
| `bms/control-flow-fixed-values.bms` | `#SETRANDOM 2` fixes the following RANDOM result, so only IF 2 is active. `#SETSWITCH 1` fixes the following SWITCH result, selecting CASE 1 while DEF remains inactive. Preserve fixed-value commands as source nodes as well as their selected projection. | Fixed values apply to the next matching RANDOM/SWITCH block; caller-supplied choices can explicitly select a block as well. |
| `bms/custom-channel.bme` | Preserve PLAYER 7 and raw channels `1A` and `31`. Do not assign custom channel `1A` to a built-in playable lane based on the extension; retain `31` as an invisible-family source channel with its exact lane suffix. | The current chart conversion is not a lossless custom-channel document model. |
| `bms/legacy-long-note.bml` | With an explicitly selected compatible lane profile, pair the two channel-51 objects (`01` at measure start, `02` at the next half-measure slot) as one hold. Preserve `#LNTYPE 1`, endpoint IDs, and exact source lines in the BMS control tree. | Channel-family 5x/6x endpoint pairing is profile-gated; LNOBJ encoding and export remain outside this fixture's coverage. |
| `bms/pms-nine-button.pms` | Resolve raw channels 11, 22, and 25 using the standard PMS 9-button map (buttons 1, 6, and 9); retain raw channel IDs for export. | The fixture defines the expected mapping; profile selection must remain explicit if evidence is ambiguous. |
| `bms/negative-undefined-resource.bms` | Reject or retain with a targeted diagnostic: channel 11 references WAV 7F, which is undefined. No invented resource may be created. | A format reader must report the missing reference rather than silently bind another asset. |
| `bms/negative-malformed-pairs.bms` | Report the odd-length channel payload; do not drop the trailing nibble or partially publish notes. Preserve raw text for repair. | Wormedit's byte-oriented parser/recovery policy is not implemented yet. |
| `bms/negative-orphan-control.bms` | Report orphan `#ENDRANDOM`; retain the raw command and surrounding program text if recovery is possible. | The current tree parser has limited all-or-error recovery; malformed tree behavior is profile-specific. |
| `stepmania/matched-timing.sm` and `stepmania/matched-timing.ssc` | These matched charts express the same fields and note rows: offset +0.125 s; BPM 120 at beat 0 and 150 at beat 8; stop 0.5 s at beat 2; delay 0.25 s at beat 3; native warp `[4,6)`; scroll -0.5 at beat 6; and a SPEEDS transition at beat 8. Keep stop and delay distinct, retain the signed offset, and compare the two documents semantically despite different chart scoping syntax. | The existing loader uses a common SM command path for these fields but converts warp data to a derived time-domain transient representation. A semantic reader/writer comparison is still required. |
| `stepmania/native-warp.ssc` | Preserve native `#WARPS:4=4` exactly as musical interval `[4,8)`, including notes that lie in its span for validation/preview. | `reinterpret_warp_data` converts SSC beat warps to a literal time-jump approximation; it does not preserve the exact source interval in its transient form. |
| `stepmania/legacy-negative-bpm.sm` | Keep the literal BPM commands 120 at beat 0, -120 at beat 4, and 120 at beat 8. Under an explicitly selected legacy conversion profile, the negative run is a warp-like interval; do not erase the source BPM run or silently equate it with native `#WARPS`. | `WarpifyTiming` makes the negative BPM positive and creates a transient time warp. For this fixture, its negative section is 4 beats at 120 BPM (2 s) and the implementation records a 4 s transient warp. This is reference behavior, not Wormedit's canonical beat-domain representation. |
| `stepmania/legacy-negative-bpm-multiple.sm` | Keep the BPM source sequence 120 at beat 0, -120 at 4, 120 at 8, -120 at 12, and 120 at 16. With the explicit `legacy_negative_bpm` source profile, canonicalize the two negative runs to exact beat-domain warps `[4,8)` and `[12,16)`, retain the original `BPMS` field/provenance, and emit one summarized legacy-encoding warning. Re-exporting through SSC's explicit `legacy_negative_stop` target profile must re-import as the same two warps. | Wormedit's paired codec tests both regions and the selected SSC legacy export/re-import. The profile names describe syntax choices, not verified support by a specific StepMania release. |
| `stepmania/legacy-negative-stop.sm` | Keep the negative STOP value -2.0 s at beat 4 as source provenance. A selected legacy profile may interpret it as a 2 s forward warp; at constant 120 BPM that is equivalent to four beats, but the canonical imported object must preserve the original time-valued encoding until the profile is chosen. | `convert_stops_to_warps` removes the negative stop and stores a transient warp of +2 s at its derived time. |
| `stepmania/stop-inside-warp.ssc` | Retain native warp `[4,8)`, stop 0.5 s and delay 0.25 s both at beat 6, plus their source ordering. Exercise the selected profile's rule for timing events inside a warp; never collapse stop and delay into one event. | The existing warp approximation explicitly does not fully handle stops inside warp spans. |
| `stepmania/discontinuity-order.ssc` | Under the explicit native-warp implementation profile, retain BPM 180, delay 0.25 s, a chart/metronome pulse, and stop 0.5 s at beat 2, plus the separate native warp `[4,5)`. The preview discontinuity stream must expose StepMania 5.1's BPM, delay, event, then stop phases without conflating events that occur before and after the delay. | The ordering is pinned against StepMania 5.1's upstream `TimingData::FindEvent`; the fixture is a focused Wormedit regression input, not an upstream conformance file. |
| `stepmania/versioned-metadata.ssc` | Exercise the v0.83 song and chart metadata inventory, including subtitle/transliterations, genre, origin, song/chart credits, banner/background/CD title, sample range, selectable/display-BPM fields, chart name/description/style, and chart-specific music. Normalized edits must round-trip without losing retained format-only fields. | The paired Wormedit codec maps chart name/credit to editable chart metadata and preserves the remaining safe source fields in their original scopes. |
| `stepmania/negative-invalid-timing.ssc` | Reject `nan` BPM as non-finite and leave no partially imported chart. | Negative fixture for numeric validation; expected independent of the legacy converter. |
| `stepmania/negative-version-0.69.ssc` | Reject v0.69 before interpreting `#WARPS:4=8`: before SSC 0.70 the second number was an absolute ending beat, while the supported 0.83 profile treats it as a relative length. No partially imported chart may be published. | StepMania 5.1 defines the semantic gates in [`NotesLoaderSSC.h`](https://github.com/stepmania/stepmania/blob/5_1-new/src/NotesLoaderSSC.h), applies the legacy warp conversion in [`NotesLoaderSSC.cpp`](https://github.com/stepmania/stepmania/blob/5_1-new/src/NotesLoaderSSC.cpp), and declares/writes 0.83 through [`Song.h`](https://github.com/stepmania/stepmania/blob/5_1-new/src/Song.h) and [`NotesWriterSSC.cpp`](https://github.com/stepmania/stepmania/blob/5_1-new/src/NotesWriterSSC.cpp). Wormedit currently supports only that audited SSC version profile; an omitted version follows StepMania 5.1's 0.83 default. |
| `osu/mania-tags-bookmarks-kiai.osu` | Accept as 4K mania. Preserve ordered tags, bookmarks 1000/2500/5000 ms, background/video/storyboard/custom-hit-sample resource references, all difficulty metadata, and absolute hit-object times. Hold spans 2500–4000 ms. Uninherited points set BPM; inherited points set SV. Kiai turns on at 1000 ms and off at 3000 ms; bit 3 and other retained timing-point fields survive edits. | The project plan does not record a complete `libotoworm` osu! field audit; this fixture defines the required Wormedit semantics without asserting parity. |

| `osu/lazer-v128-fractional.osu` | Accept the lazer-v128 profile, retain `osu.file_format = 128`, and preserve fractional tap/hold timestamps `1000.5`, `1200.5`, and `1400.5` without the stable-v14 integer-millisecond quantization. Default re-export retains v128; an explicit stable-v14 conversion rounds with a typed loss diagnostic. | At pinned official osu! revision `ebaf7e9910ef3755308dec2c7950d916aabc545b`, the [lazer encoder](https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/ebaf7e9910ef3755308dec2c7950d916aabc545b/osu.Game/Beatmaps/Formats/LegacyBeatmapEncoder.cs) declares v128 and writes `double` start/end times, while the [decoder](https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/ebaf7e9910ef3755308dec2c7950d916aabc545b/osu.Game/Beatmaps/Formats/LegacyBeatmapDecoder.cs) dispatches from the declared version. The fixture isolates the audited mania timing distinction rather than claiming every lazer-only non-mania construct. |
| `bmson/slicing-and-mixed-sounds.bmson` | Resolution 240 maps naturally to 960 editor rows per 4/4 measure. Lines at 0, 960, and 1680 encode one standard bar and then a 3/4-length bar. In `long-voice.ogg`, pulse 0 restarts, 240 and 480 continue, the hold at 480 has length 240, and pulse 960 restarts. In `snare.wav`, the BGM event at pulse 240 shares its derived slice with playable x=3; BMSON's playable-over-BGM rule removes the redundant BGM event. Keep x=5 hold at 960 length 480 and simultaneous distinct sound channels layered. | The current library conversion discards BMSON slicing, sound-channel order, BGM events, measure lengths, and source metadata before the editor receives the chart. |
| `bmson/published-vox-slicing.bmson` | Normative BMSON 1.0 slicing example at BPM 120. Distinct pulses 240/360/720/840/1200/1680 produce source ranges 0–0.25 s, 0.25–1 s, 1–1.25 s, 1.25–2 s, 2–3 s, and 3 s–EOF. Same-pulse notes share a slice; pulses 240 and 720 restart, while the others continue. The final x=0 event remains BGM. | This is the specification's published `vox.wav` sequence converted from its concise YAML notation to valid JSON. It is the normative writer/evaluator oracle. |
| `bmson/zero-resolution-default.bmson` | BMSON 1.0 defines explicit zero, null, or omitted resolution as the default 240 pulses per quarter note. Import at 240 and retain the original zero spelling/provenance for a stable source round trip. | This is a spec edge case rather than invalid input. An earlier draft treated zero as invalid; [`bmsone-slicing.md`](../../docs/references/bmsone-slicing.md) now records the corrected normative rule. |
| `bmson/null-resolution-default.bmson` | Apply the normative 240 default to an explicit JSON null and retain that the source used null. | Paired with zero and omission so all three default spellings have an oracle. |
| `bmson/omitted-resolution-default.bmson` | Apply the normative 240 default when `info.resolution` is absent and retain that the field was absent. | Paired with zero and null so all three default spellings have an oracle. |
| `bmson/negative-wrong-resolution-type.bmson` | Reject the string-valued resolution as a type error; do not coerce it to 240. | The reader must validate JSON field types before pulse mapping. |
| `bmson/negative-pulse-position.bmson` | Reject `y = -1`; BMSON pulse positions are unsigned integers. Do not clamp to zero. | The reader must validate event numbers before timing conversion. |
| `bmson/negative-fractional-pulse-position.bmson` | Reject non-integral `y = 1.5`; never round a source pulse while importing. | The reader must preserve exact integer pulse semantics. |
| `bmson/negative-overflow-pulse-position.bmson` | Reject `y = 4294967296` as outside BMSON 1.0's Web IDL `unsigned long` range without wrapping, truncating, or passing through binary floating point. | The JSON and timing layers need checked integer parsing. |
| `bmson/conflicting-continuation-flags.bmson` | At pulse 240, conflicting `c` flags resolve to restart (`false`) for the shared slice, as BMSON 1.0 specifies. Notes on x=1 and x=2 share one derived slice. Pulse 480 continues from that restarted source position. | The editor should retain both source flags and expose the normalized restart result; it must not choose by note ordering. |

## Coverage boundaries

This Stage 0 slice covers hand-authored text cases for the immediate parser and timing work: BMS/BME/BML/PMS, mixed and fixed BMS control flow, byte-authored BMS encoding cases (documented in [`bms/encoding/README.md`](bms/encoding/README.md)), SM/SSC matched timing, native/legacy warp encodings including repeated negative-BPM regions, and explicit SSC version boundaries, osu!mania metadata/resources/kiai, and BMSON bar lines/slices/mixed sounds. The BMSON `vox.wav` case is the specification's published data sequence transcribed from YAML to JSON. The paired SM/SSC case is a matched input comparison, not proof that every StepMania feature is accepted by every player. Compatibility results must name the parser/writer profile; current timing profile names identify explicit syntax policies and are not release-level compatibility claims. BMSON expectations follow the [BMSON 1.0 specification](https://github.com/bemusic/bmson-spec/blob/master/doc/index.rst), including its zero-resolution default and duplicate continuation-flag rule.

The complete built-in BMS-family lane-map matrix has a separate, smaller [profile fixture
inventory](bms/profiles/README.md). Load that inventory only for lane-profile or BMS dialect work.

The audio directory contains synthetic tones, a polyphonic source, silence, and a longer seek/stream sample; it does not contain recorded audio. The corpus does not yet contain clipboard captures, exhaustive automatic BMS profile-detection combinations, or a full published BMSON sample with media. The synthetic video fixture is inventoried separately under `video/`. No fixture should be described as passing a reader/writer test until a harness asserts its expected semantics.
